ground_truth.description: When a session call with BEHAVIOR_REVERT_ON_ERROR fails, the transaction reverts but nonce is not consumed. The signature remains valid and can be replayed for partial calls. Session signatures are validated per-call using individual call hashes, enabling partial replay. Frontrunners can execute subsets of calls to grief or cause financial loss.
ground_truth.root_cause: When a session call with BEHAVIOR_REVERT_ON_ERROR fails, the transaction reverts but nonce is not consumed. The signature remains valid and can be replayed for partial calls. Session signatures are validated per-call using individual call hashes, enabling partial replay. Frontrunners can execute subsets of calls to grief or cause financial loss.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Original payload: Calls [A, B, C] with signatures [SigA, SigB, SigC]. Execution: [A succeed, B succeed, C revert]. Result: Revert, nonce unused. Attack: Replay [A, B] with [SigA, SigB]. PoC: File POC.t.sol with test testSubmissionValidity. It builds a 2-call payload, expects revert on second call, then replays partial payload successfully.
ground_truth.fix_description: Bind session call signatures to the complete payload hash to prevent partial signature replay.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The contract validates signatures per-call rather than per-payload. When a call with BEHAVIOR_REVERT_ON_ERROR fails, the transaction reverts but the nonce is not consumed (nonce consumption happens before execution). This leaves the signature valid for partial replay attacks. Attackers can execute subsets of calls from a signed payload.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. User signs payload with calls [A, B, C] where B will fail with BEHAVIOR_REVERT_ON_ERROR. 2. Attacker frontruns execution, extracts signature. 3. Attacker creates new payload with only call A (profitable call). 4. Attacker submits this partial payload with original signature. 5. Signature validates successfully since it's per-call based. 6. Attacker steals value from call A without executing B or C.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Bind signatures to the complete payload hash instead of individual call hashes. Modify signatureValidation to hash the entire payload including all calls. Ensure nonce consumption happens after successful execution or implement signature invalidation on partial failures.

prediction.overall_explanation: The contract has a critical signature replay vulnerability where partial execution of signed payloads is possible. The root cause is per-call signature validation combined with nonce consumption before execution. This enables frontrunning attacks where attackers can extract profitable calls from multi-call transactions while discarding unprofitable ones. The vulnerability is exploitable without trusted role compromise and can lead to direct financial loss.
